gui.until_eternity.lore_book.miner_log.p: End Calendar, Year 742, June 19
June 19, continued

The ore vein was strange today.

We were mining aether ore beneath the outer islands. Shaft Six was already deep. The foreman said another twenty blocks down should bring us to a rich vein.

We did find something.

But it was not ore.

When the pickaxe broke through the last layer of end stone, a sound came from below.

It was not rock splitting, nor silverfish crawling.

It sounded as if... something was breathing.

Very slowly.

Very deeply.

Every time I heard it, my chest tightened.

The foreman told us to stop, but Karn would not listen. He said there was only a hollow below and mocked us for spending so long in the End that we had become afraid of stones.

Then he broke that stone open.

There was no cave below.

Only a stretch of black.

Not the void we usually see.

The void, at least, is quiet.

That thing was not.

It was moving.
The Twentieth Day
The Twentieth Day, continued

We sealed off Shaft Six.

No one slept well last night.

Karn kept saying he heard someone calling his name.

None of us could hear it.

This morning, he was gone.

The foreman took several people to look for him.

After a long time, they returned.

Karn returned too.

But I do not know if he could still be called Karn.

Black things had grown on his arms, like veins or the roots of some plant. His purple eyes had grown so dark they were almost invisible.

He simply stood there.

Motionless.

The foreman asked him what had happened.

Karn raised his head.

Then he smiled.

I have never seen a person smile like that.
The Twenty-First Day
The Twenty-First Day, continued

The mine has been closed.

It is already too late.

Karn attacked the foreman.

We tried to restrain him, but when we drew near, his body suddenly twisted.

It was not teleportation.

I know what teleportation looks like.

It was more as though something tore his body apart and assembled it again somewhere else.

Afterward, everyone he had touched began to show the same symptoms.

First came silence.

Then their skin turned black.

Then they began staring into the depths of the mine.

No matter how we called to them, they did not answer.

They would say only one thing.
"There is still room below."
I do not know what that means.
The Twenty-Second Day
The Twenty-Second Day, continued

The mine has fallen.

I saw my own people kill the guards.

No.

I cannot call them my people.

Those things are no longer my kin.

Black corrosion covers their bodies. Some have arms stretched unnaturally long. Others have chests split open, with no blood inside, only a darkness that churns ceaselessly like mist.

Worst of all, they can still teleport.

And faster than before.

Walls are useless.

Doors are useless too.

We fled into the storage area and blocked the entrance with every piece of end stone we could find.

It has been quiet outside for a long time.

I would rather they made a sound.

At least then I would know where they are.
I Do Not Know the Day
Unknown Day, continued

The lamp is about to go out.

There are three chorus fruits left.

I dare not eat them.

If I teleport out, I do not know where I will land.

Now and then I hear a pickaxe striking stone outside.

Once.

Once.

And once again.

They are still mining.

Just as they used to.

Sometimes I almost imagine that nothing happened at all.

The foreman would still scold us for slacking at shift change. Karn would secretly hide the finest aether ore. We would gather by the lift shaft to argue about who would take the deepest passage that day.

But I know it is not so.

Because the blows of that pickaxe are coming closer and closer.
Later
Later, continued

I understand now.

They are not looking for me.

They are still digging downward.

The thing beneath Shaft Six is still there.

My corroded kin are only its tools.

So are we.

Perhaps it has been waiting for us since the first time we swung a pickaxe here.

We thought we were mining the End.

But the thing beneath the End was using our hands to dig itself out.

If anyone finds this diary—

Do not take the ore from this place.

Do not go near Shaft Six.

Do not trust any of my kin who can still speak.

If you hear breathing beneath the stone,
Do not keep digging.

...

Wait.

The pickaxe has stopped outside.

They have stopped.

I hear someone standing beyond the door.

It is calling my name.

The voice is Karn's.

He says—
"We found it."
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.author: Scylla
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.1.1: They have crossed the Sea of Thunder.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.1.2: I killed wave after wave of divine envoys, sank their warships, and called down lightning upon those gods who claimed to be eternal.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.1.3: Yet the enemy kept growing in number.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.1.4: I defended one city, and they destroyed another.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.1.5: I saved one legion, only to see black smoke rising from the burning royal city in the distance.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.1.6: For the first time, I felt how small my power truly was.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.2.2: The soldiers are all dead, and the palace is burning.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.2.3: I do not know what I am still defending.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.2.4: Perhaps I simply refuse to admit that we lost.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.2.7: I can still wield a weapon, summon storms, and kill the enemies who enter the capital.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.2.9: Until I could no longer hear the voices of my people.
book.until_eternity.damp_diary.entry.2.1: But the Storm Dynasty is dead.
I once believed that if I had the power to defy the gods, I could protect all of this.
Now I understand—I can kill gods, but I cannot save my dynasty.
gui.until_eternity.lore_book.torn_paper_: The empty armor passes the north cistern every forty breaths. After the third bell it stops at the broken crest.
Margin: its reflection turns before the armor does.
The lead copy broke in the lock. The true key was moved from the western box to the third drain.
Cast no more. The lock hears echoes in the metal.
Lower the north pool, then light three old lamps in reverse: west, east, south. Stop at the crest's lower edge.
Never light the fourth. It is not a lamp. It is a bolt.
There are no bodies in the armor. They are echoes of the old ward, repeating the route of its final night.
While the echoes still patrol, the thing beneath the altar is not fully awake.
Five corners point to a sealed stair below the third drain. Someone behind it now prays in my voice.
Burn the map. Throw the key back into the water. Stop here.
